findings.title: MCP11: OAuth proxy lacks per-client consent
findings.description: OAuth proxy flow does not show per-client consent, state, and client binding controls.
findings.recommendation: Bind consent and OAuth state to each client_id and exactly validate redirect_uri.

findings.title: MCP15: Authorization URL handled unsafely
findings.description: A dynamic authorization URL is opened without visible scheme validation.
findings.recommendation: Allow only HTTPS (or development loopback HTTP) and never open URLs through a shell.

findings.title: MCP04: Unpinned or mutable dependency

findings.recommendation: Pin exact versions and commit hashes and commit the corresponding lockfile.

findings.title: MCP09: Unmanaged server registration
findings.description: MCP server configuration executes a mutable or unpinned package/source.
findings.recommendation: Pin the package/version or immutable commit and record it in the approved server inventory.

findings.title: MCP07: Network server lacks visible authorization
findings.description: A network-capable MCP transport has no visible authentication or authorization enforcement.
findings.recommendation: Authenticate every request and authorize each tool/resource operation.

findings.title: MCP01: Secret included in output or logs

findings.recommendation: Redact credentials and never place them in tool output, model context, or logs.

findings.title: Prompt Injection Risk: External data embedded in f-string
findings.description: External data is returned without apparent sanitization. This could allow injected content to manipulate the LLM.
findings.recommendation: Avoid embedding external data in f-strings that become part of LLM context. Use separate data fields with clear boundaries.
